must_fix.title: Slotted targets get hidden: wrapper around the <slot> showing a light-DOM target is set aria-hidden
must_fix.evidence:
With enableShadowDOM(), host shadow root '
Header
' and the target as a light child of host; after ariaHideOutside([target]) the probe printed 'header true wrap true slot null'. #wrap, which renders the slotted target in the composed tree that screen readers read, is aria-hidden, so the target is hidden. walkTree (src/ariaHideOutside.ts) walks host.shadowRoot because the host contains the target, and walk/acceptNode uses nodeContains, which follows parentNode, not assignedSlot. Before this change walk(root) never entered the shadow root. No test covers slots.

nits: Shadow roots found while handling a mutation (walkTree in the MutationObserver) are walked but never observed, so content added later inside a newly added shadow root (e.g. one holding a live announcer, whose host stays visible) is not hidden.

Tests are in a separate ariaHideOutside.shadow.test.js; other packages put shadow DOM tests in a describe block that calls enableShadowDOM() in the existing test file (FocusScope.test.js:2011, usePress.test.js:3993). Keeping them separate is defensible because the flag can't be turned off.
getShadowRootsWithin(root) runs querySelectorAll('*') recursively over the whole document on every call, and again for every added node in the observer, which is costly on large pages.

report:
I'm not merging this yet. Tests, lint and the type check all pass, but there is one confirmed regression: when shadow DOM support is on, a target placed in a light-DOM element and shown through a `` (a web component's slot) gets hidden. **Checks I ran (all pass):** - `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays`: 11 suites, 200 tests passed. This includes the new `ariaHideOutside.shadow.test.js`. - `yarn eslint packages/@react-aria/overlays`: no errors. - `yarn check-types`: no errors. **Must fix: slotted targets get hidden.** With the flag on, `walkTree` walks the shadow root of any host that contains a visible node. It decides what to keep visible with `nodeContains(node, target)`, and that check follows parent nodes, not slot assignment. So the wrapper around the `` that renders the target counts as "outside" and gets `aria-hidden="true"`. Screen readers read the composed (flattened) tree, in which that wrapper is an ancestor of the target, so the target itself is hidden. I reproduced it with a temporary probe test in `packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/` (deleted afterwards): ```js enableShadowDOM(); let host = document.createElement('div'); document.body.appendChild(host); let sr = host.attachShadow({mode: 'open'}); sr.innerHTML = '
Header
'; let target = document.createElement('button'); host.appendChild(target); ariaHideOutside([target]); console.log('header', …'#h'…, 'wrap', …'#wrap'…, 'slot', …) ``` Output: ``` header true wrap true slot null ``` `#wrap` holds the `` that renders the target, and it is now `aria-hidden="true"`. Before this change the light-DOM-only `walk(root)` never entered the shadow root, so the target stayed exposed. This is the shadow DOM setup the issue is about, and it breaks the first requirement: everything outside the targets is hidden, not the targets. No test covers slots. **Other edge cases I tried, which behave correctly:** - Nested calls inside the same shadow root. - Restoring after nested calls. - Hosts added later inside a target's shadow root. - With the flag off, `walkTree(node, [])` does the same thing as the old `walk`. The PR adds `@react-stately/flags` to `package.json` and `yarn.lock` correctly, there are no unrelated edits, and `git status` is as I found it. ```json {"mergeable": false, "must_fix": [{"title": "Slotted targets get hidden: wrapper around the showing a light-DOM target is set aria-hidden", "kind": "regression", "evidence": "With enableShadowDOM(), host shadow root '
